result.reason: All three items form the continuous Avidarna story — Rav Yehuda's gift, Rav Yosef's challenge about formal ger toshav status, and the circumcision objection with its resolution — which is precisely what the 'Avidrana Gift Story' prose describes.

The passage describes Rava bringing a gift to Bar Sheishach on a festival day with the justification that he doesn't worship idols, then finding him in the rose water scene — content that matches heading 6 ('Gift on Holiday') which explicitly discusses Rava presenting a gift to Bar Sheishach on a pagan holiday and the subsequent discovery, rather than heading 7 which only covers the rose water scene already in progress.

The passage describes the royal messenger arriving and Bar Sheshakh being summoned by the king, which matches exactly the 'King's Messenger' section's prose about the pristaka arriving and the king requiring Bar Sheshakh — the eye-bursting detail is a brief coda that follows naturally, and the 'Blessing & Blinded Eye' section's prose separately covers that moment as its own focus.

The passage contains exactly the statements by Rav Pappi and Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak about alternative verses Rava should have cited, which is precisely what the 'Alternative Verses' section prose discusses.

The passage specifically discusses the mishna's implication that wages are permitted even without a nightfall ('l'tutei erev') specification, which directly corresponds to the 'Nightfall Request' section's prose about the tension between the Tosefta's nightfall qualification and the Mishna's broader permission.

All three items form the continuous Gemara discussion of the lump-sum vs. per-barrel payment distinction (the baraita raising the contradiction, Abaye and Rava's resolutions, and the confirming baraita), which is precisely what the 'Lump Sum Problem' prose describes.

The passage discusses why the donkey rental clause needs to be stated and introduces the latter clause about riding (not transporting wine), which is exactly what the 'Animal Rental' prose describes — the Gemara's question about redundancy and the resolution that the end of the Mishnah requires statement.

All five items form a continuous Talmudic discussion about the renter's right to place a jug on a donkey and the distinction between renter's and donkey driver's provisioning rights, which is precisely what the 'Donkey Driver Rights' prose describes in detail.

Both items together form the opening narrative of the wine-pouring story — the father of Rav Aḥa son of Rav Ika pouring wine and ferrying gentiles, and Abaye's ki katrach be-heteira ruling — which is precisely what the 'Wine Pouring Story' prose describes.

Both items are part of the same Gemara discussion about rotzeh be-kiyumo and ferrying wine across a crossing, which is precisely what the prose under heading 0 ('Heteira & Rotzeh') describes in detail.

All three items — the Mishnah about wine on figs/dates with the Boethus ben Zunen incident, the concluding principle about beneficial vs. detrimental taste, and the Gemara's resolution that the Mishnah is incomplete (*chisore mekhsara*) — are precisely what the 'Veitos Ben Zonam' prose describes, making the current placement correct.
All three items together form the Rava wheat-sale ruling and the kil'ayim-garment objection raised by Rabbah bar Livai, which is precisely the content described in the 'Wheat Sale Ruling' prose.

The passage describes Rava's retraction and his ruling to permit grinding, baking, and selling to gentiles not in Jewish presence, which exactly matches the 'Bread Solution' section's prose discussing this same ruling and its rationale.
